questions.question: You want to compare the mean exam scores of four different schools. Which test is the right starting point?
questions.explanation: One-way ANOVA tests all four means in a single test. Running six t-tests would inflate the chance of a false alarm.

questions.question: If you run three independent t-tests, each at α = 0.05, when no real differences exist, roughly how likely is at least one false alarm?
questions.explanation: 1 − 0.95³ ≈ 0.143, so about 14%. The more comparisons, the worse it gets.

questions.question: In ANOVA, F = MSB ÷ MSW. What does a value of F near 1 suggest?
options: The group means are very different
The gaps between group means are about what the scatter inside the groups would produce
questions.explanation: MSW measures noise inside groups. If MSB is about the same size, the group means are no more spread out than noise alone would make them.

questions.question: Three groups of 5 give SSB = 792.1 and SSW = 110.8. What are the degrees of freedom for the F test?
questions.explanation: df between = k − 1 = 2. df within = N − k = 15 − 3 = 12. The numerator df comes first.

questions.question: With SSB = 792.1, SSW = 110.8, df = (2, 12), what is F?
A one-way ANOVA is significant (p = 0.001) for three treatments. What can you conclude?
options: All three treatments differ from each other
At least one treatment mean differs from the others
questions.explanation: ANOVA is an omnibus test. It says that some difference exists, not which pairs differ. A post-hoc test such as Tukey's HSD finds the specific pairs.

questions.question: You will test all 6 pairs among 4 groups with a Bonferroni correction at an overall α of 0.05. What α do you use for each pair?
questions.explanation: Bonferroni divides α by the number of comparisons: 0.05 ÷ 6 ≈ 0.0083.

questions.question: SSB = 450 and SST = 1,800. What is η² and what does it mean?
options: 0.25: 25% of the variation is linked to group membership
0.75: 75% of the variation is linked to group membership
questions.explanation: η² = SSB ÷ SST = 450 ÷ 1,800 = 0.25. A quarter of the total variation lines up with the groups, which is a large effect by the usual guide (0.14 and up).
